item.title: GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
item.description:
Voting
GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
Updated November 13, 20269:34 PM ET
Originally published November 13, 20265:18 PM ET
Hansi Lo Wang
An election worker sorts mail-in ballots at the Miami-Dade County Supervisor of Elections Office in Doral for Florida's primary election in August.
Lynne Sladky/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Lynne Sladky/AP
Voting for this year's midterm elections just concluded, but Republican officials in a number of states are already looking to shape how votes are cast in 2028.
Twelve GOP state attorneys general are pushing to revive the president's bid for mail-in voting restrictions in time for the 2028 election.
On Thursday, they started the process of appealing a September order by U.S. District Judge Carl Nichols, one of the two judges who blocked the U.S. Postal Service from carrying out a plan released in response to an executive order by President Trump.

The nationwide ground stop that paralyzed the U.S. aviation system on Friday has ended, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.
The rare stop, which lasted about four hours, grounded thousands of flights at all U.S. airports in one of the biggest disruptions of the nation's air travel system since the September 11th attacks.
In a Friday night news conference, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that air traffic control facilities had experienced "intermittent" outages of their radar and communications systems beginning earlier in the afternoon. Duffy blamed outdated technology for the failures.

item.title: What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
item.description:
What's Trump's strategy now with Iran? To keep things as they are
November 13, 20262:02 PM ET
Aya Batrawy
Mourners carry coffins during the funeral of people killed in recent airstrikes on al-Shariya village, northeast of Sanaa, which Houthi authorities blamed on Saudi Arabia, in Houthi-controlled Sanaa, Yemen, Nov. 11, 2026.
Osamah Abdulrahman/AP
hide caption
toggle caption i
Osamah Abdulrahman/AP
DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — President Trump is confronting new realities nine months into the war with Iran that leave him with dwindling options to ending the conflict.
On Thursday, he waved away the need for a deal with Iran, saying the U.S. has billions of Iran's dollars frozen in overseas accounts.
"We don't need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed. We've got their money," he wrote in a Truth Social post.
Negotiations with Iran are stuck with mediator Qatar working to bridge the divide. Trump met Qatar's prime minister at the White House this week, and said afterward that Gulf Arab allies prefer "the status quo" of continued economic pressure on Iran. He wrote that while the U.S. remains "locked and loaded," an attack at this point "seems to be quite unlikely."

The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
Updated November 13, 20262:31 PM ET
Originally published November 13, 202612:00 PM ET
By
Jude Joffe-Block
Election workers process vote-by-mail ballots at the Los Angeles County Ballot Processing Center on Nov. 5.
Mario Tama/Getty Images
hide caption
toggle caption i
Mario Tama/Getty Images
In the weeks before Election Day, the Trump administration escalated its hunt for voter fraud and its pressure on election officials — especially in California — to crack down on illegal voting by non-U.S. citizens.
Now, with Election Day come and gone, election officials and civil rights attorneys are preparing for the administration to continue its search for noncitizens on state voter rolls, as well as what they see as intimidation tactics toward election officials.
"It's clear that there is this drive to try to conjure up facts that just don't exist. I don't think that's going to change," James Williams, county executive for California's Santa Clara County, told NPR. "So we fully are prepared to continue to deal with this."
